card.statement:
Suppose that $\bfC$ is an $\bfA$-algebra. Recall a Frobenius structure of $\bfC$ (see <<cite:Lurie.higher.algebra>>) is an $\bfA$-module functor $\la: \bfC\to \bfA$ such that the composed functor

\[
\bfC\otimes_\bfA\bfC\xrightarrow{m} \bfC\xrightarrow{\la} \bfA
\]

forms the co-unit map in the duality datum of $\bfC$.
Therefore, it induces an $\bfA$-module equivalence

\[
\verd^\la: \bfC^\vee\cong \bfC,
\]

such that $e_\bfC(c\boxtimes_{\bfA}d)=\la(c\otimes \verd^{\la}(d))$ for every $c\in \bfC$ and every $d\in \bfC^\vee$.
Then the functor

\[
\bfC^{\op}\to \bfC^\vee\xrightarrow{\verd^\la} \bfC, \quad c\mapsto \verd^\la(c^*)
\]

takes a more familiar form as follows. For simplicity, we write $c^{*,\la}$ instead of $\verd^\la(c^{*})$.
Let $\omega^\la\in \bfC$ that represents the functor

\[
\bfC^{\op}\to \bfA, \quad c\mapsto \Map_\bfA(\la(c),\mathbf{1}_\bfA).
\]

Then

\begin{multline*}
\Map_{\bfC}(d,\verd^\la(c^*))\cong\Map_{\bfC^\vee}((\verd^\la)^{-1}(d),c^*)\cong\Map_{\bfA}(e_\bfC(c\boxtimes_{\bfA} (\verd^\la)^{-1}(d)),\mathbf{1}_\bfA)\\
\cong\Map_{\bfA}(\la(c\otimes d),\mathbf{1}_\bfA)= \Map_{\bfA}(\la(d\otimes \sigma_\la(c)),\mathbf{1}_\bfA) =\Map_{\bfC}(d\otimes \sigma_\la(c), \omega^\la).
\end{multline*}

Here

\begin{equation}
\sigma_\la: \bfC\to \bfC,
\end{equation}

is the Serre automorphism associated to the Frobenius algebra $(\bfC,\la)$,
which is a monoidal automorphism of $\bfC$ (see <<cite:Lurie.higher.algebra>>), characterized such that $\la(a\otimes b)\cong \la(b\otimes \sigma_\la(a))$ for every $a,b\in \bfC$.

Therefore,

\begin{equation}
c^{*,\la}=\underline\Hom(\sigma_\la(c),\omega^\la).
\end{equation}

In particular, if $\bfC=\bfA$ with the Frobenius structure given by $\la=\id_\bfA$, then

\begin{equation}
c^{*,\id}=\underline\Hom(c,\mathbf{1}_\bfA).
\end{equation}
card.label: Example 466

paper.title: Tame categorical local Langlands correspondence
paper.abstract: In one of our previous articles, we outlined the formulation of a version of the categorical arithmetic local Langlands conjecture. The aims of this article are threefold. First, we provide a detailed account of one component of this conjecture: the local Langlands category. Second, we aim to prove this conjecture in the tame case for quasi-split unramified reductive groups. Finally, we will explore the first applications of such categorical equivalence.
